title: Zephyr Med SOC2 / ISO27001 posture & trust center access sync
summary: High-level SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review: verified Trust Center artifacts available, discussed RBAC/SSO model for private deployment, KMS/encryption flows, audit log retention and data residency constraints. Agreed to do a short KMS POC and a mapping doc for controls. Action items assigned to SE and Zephyr compliance. Next call to review evidence ingestion plan.
next_steps: Priya to run KMS POC against Zephyr staging VPC and share runbook (due 2027-11-25)
Jordan to send Trust Center link and SOC2 report extract examples
Zephyr to share control owner matrix for mapping by 2027-11-24
Schedule follow-up with legal for contract scoping week of 2027-11-29
action_items: Priya Nair (SE): Perform KMS integration POC (wrap keys with customer KMS) using Zephyr staging creds; due 2027-11-25
Maya Alvarez (Zephyr): Send control-owner matrix and high-level scope of in-scope systems; due 2027-11-24
Jordan Kim (AE): Share Trust Center link, recent SOC 2 summary, and data residency whitepaper; due 2027-11-19
Tom Hsu (Zephyr DevOps): Provide sample audit log slice and retention policy; due 2027-11-22
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-18 15:00 PT | Duration ~52m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Luis (Redwood); Maya, Ethan, Rita, Tom, Olivia (Zephyr)

[00:00] Jordan: All right folks, thanks for joining. uh this is Jordan from Redwood, AE. quick intro, priya is our SE who will drive the technical bits. Luis on CS. Maya, do you want to kick off with the posture questions?
[00:12] Maya: Yeah thanks Jordan. We want to understand what artifacts you can expose in the Trust Center and how that maps to SOC 2 and ISO 27001, plus specifics on RBAC/SAML flows for a private deployment in our VPC. Also KMS, how keys are handled and audit logs.
[00:30] Priya: Great, I'll try to run through what we have. Quick note, some of the doc names in the trust center sometimes show older model names, uh transcription may spell things odd. But the artifacts we provide: SOC 2 Type II report summary, ISO scope statement, pen-test summary (redacted), system architecture diagrams, and a controls matrix export.
[00:52] Ethan: On the controls matrix, can you give an example mapping? We have a custom app that stores PHI, so we need clarity on control ownership and evidence collection.
[01:05] Priya: Sure. We typically deliver a csv with controls rows mapped to Redwood controls, then a column indicating customer evidence needed. We'll pre-fill things where Redwood is responsible (like network segregation, encryption at rest) and leave customer evidence for app-level access controls. We'll also mark which controls map to SOC 2 CC6x and ISO A.5/A.6 etc.
[01:28] Rita: Are those csv exports accessible via the Trust Center or do you need to send them manually?
[01:34] Jordan: The default is Trust Center access. We can grant a read-only link to download the matrix and the redacted reports. For enterprise customers we also support SSO-protected access.
[01:42] Tom: SSO—do you support SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning? We have an Okta-backed flow.
[01:48] Priya: Yes, SAML 2.0 and SCIM are supported. For Private deployments, we can integrate with your IdP. There are two patterns: 1) customer-managed SSO where the customer's IdP issues assertions directly to the private control plane, or 2) a managed SSO where we act as an SP and you delegate groups. The private control plane option requires some ingress rules in your VPC.
[02:12] Maya: For RBAC we need role separation—audit reader, ops, admin, developer. Is there out-of-box role mapping we can apply?
[02:20] Priya: Yes default roles exist, and you can map IdP groups to those roles. We also support custom roles if you need fine-grained permissions. Note: some lower-level runtime controls for model routing remain at ops-level by default.
[02:35] Jordan: Quick interjection: on the KMS side, Zephyr wants to ensure customer keys never leave their HSM. Priya, we talked about envelope encryption, can you restate?
[02:44] Priya: Right, envelope encryption is how we do it: Redwood encrypts data with a data key, which is itself wrapped with customer KMS (customer-managed key). We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS. For on-prem HSMs we do a key-unwrap flow via our gateway; depends on network config. The important bit is that the plaintext data key is never persistently stored outside the runtime; wrapped keys are stored.
[03:12] Ethan: So in the flow, do you ever have plaintext keys in your control plane logs? We need to confirm no, and that audit trails show key usage only as key-id references.
[03:21] Priya: Correct, we log key-id usage and operations, not plaintext. Audit logs include KMS call metadata, timestamps, and the call status. We do not log key material.
[03:29] Olivia: From legal perspective, we also want to know about evidence collection for ISO 27001 Annex A control tests—how do you provide sampling evidence?
[03:37] Luis: We have a playbook—samples of change management tickets, patching windows, configuration screenshots, and access lists. For ISO, we can generate evidence bundles per control with redaction for sensitive values.
[03:47] Maya: What about retention on audit logs? We have to retain for 7 years for certain regs.
[03:53] Priya: Default retention in Redwood hosted is 90 days for high-detailed logs, with aggregated metrics retained longer. For enterprise / dedicated we support configurable retention and long-term export to your S3 or GCS bucket for archival. For Private deployments everything stays in your VPC and you control retention.
[04:12] Tom: Can we configure push-based export rather than pull? Our infra prefers push to our Kinesis/SQS.
[04:18] Priya: Yes, we can push to S3/GCS or stream to your destination. For push to Kinesis we typically use a connector—there might be a small agent on your side. We'll capture a sample config in the runbook.
[04:29] Rita: Data residency: we need EU-only residency for PHI-related processing. If we use Redwood private in our Azure EU region, does any data transit through US control plane?
[04:41] Jordan: For Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed in their VPC/region; Redwood control plane endpoints can be regionalized. We have a pattern where control-plane metadata may route to region-specific control endpoints, not US by default; we'll confirm. For hosted we do have region pinning options but there could be some metadata tier. We'll follow up with a definitive data-flow diagram.
[05:02] Maya: On SOC 2 reports—are those full reports or only summaries? We cannot share full SOC 2 to everyone.
[05:08] Jordan: Trust Center provides a redacted SOC 2 summary for general access and full reports under NDA via secure transfer. We can also provide a SOC 2 bridge letter if needed.
[05:18] Olivia: We will likely need NDA'd full report for legal review.
[05:21] Jordan: Noted. We'll attach the NDA flow and typical timeline.
[05:25] [06:00] -- mid-call technical deep dive --
[06:00] Priya: I want to walk through a KMS POC plan quickly: we'll request a short-lived staging key or an IAM role in your staging account; we'll demonstrate wrap/unwrap, show logs, and then export log artifacts. Ideally this is a 2-3 hour lab that we run together.
[06:18] Ethan: That works. Is there any special network requirement? We run private subnets without NAT for some pieces.
[06:25] Priya: For the runtime to call your KMS, we can run an egress path through a private VPC endpoint or peered endpoint. If you want zero egress, we can run a local connector pattern that executes inside your network and proxies KMS calls. We'll document both.
[06:42] Tom: What about performance impact—does envelope decrypt/add latency? We need 99th percentile latency guarantees for inference.
[06:50] Priya: Envelope ops add negligible ms for key unwrap per session—most inference latency is dominated by model tokens. We cache unwrapped data keys in memory for the runtime session to avoid repeated unwraps. For long-running sessions we benchmarked <5ms extra for unwraps typically. We'll share micro-benchmarks.
[07:07] Maya: Okay on controls mapping, Rita will coordinate. What we want is a mapping doc that shows for each SOC 2 control where Redwood provides evidence versus where Zephyr must supply artifacts.
[07:18] Rita: I'll produce the control-owner matrix. We'll include who the evidence owner is and expected artifact format.
[07:24] Jordan: Great, we'll pre-seed that matrix with our defaults so you can just adjust.
[07:28] [15:12] -- a pause while files are checked --
[15:12] Priya: Quick note about logs: our audit logs include user activity (login, role changes), admin API calls (create model, rollout), and runtime events. We can separate PII from logs via redaction rules.
[15:25] Ethan: How granular are runtime events? Do they show prompt contents? We cannot have PHI surfaced in logs.
[15:33] Priya: By default prompts are not stored in debug logs. Some trace logs can include tokens for debugging if you enable them; but for enterprise we keep prompt content out of logs and only store sanitized metadata (lengths, token counts). We also support hashed prompt fingerprints for QA.
[15:53] Maya: Is there a way to auto-mask PHI from prompts before ingestion?
[15:58] Priya: We have a pre-ingest redaction hook you can run in your edge proxy — it can strip or tokenise PHI. For Private we can ship a small redaction lambda example.
[16:08] Olivia: Liability question: if a developer accidentally sends PHI in a prompt, how is that handled?
[16:13] Jordan: That goes into contract language and DPA terms. We can include obligations and an incident response flow. Also we can enable immediate sync to your data loss detection tooling.
[16:24] Tom: Back to SSO: for SCIM provisioning do you support group attributes sync for nested groups? Our Okta setup uses nested groups heavily.
[16:34] Priya: SCIM supports group sync but nested groups complexity depends on IdP behavior. We typically advise flattening groups for SCIM mapping, or map at role level. We'll provide a guide for Okta nested groups.
[16:47] Maya: Any known gaps against ISO Annex A for encryption key lifecycle?
[16:52] Priya: No major gaps; our lifecycle covers generation, distribution (wrapped keys), rotation policies and destruction. For certification time we can supply key rotation logs. If you require HSM attestation reports we can coordinate with the cloud provider to surface that.
[17:07] Jordan: Competitor note—OctantSec had a different model where customer keys are stored in a third vault service they host; some customers prefer our envelope approach because it reduces key-handling surface.
[17:18] Maya: good.
[17:20] [42:00] -- closing and recap --
[42:00] Jordan: Recap: Priya to run KMS POC with Tom/Ethan in staging; Jordan will share Trust Center link and redacted SOC 2 summary; Rita/Maya to send control-owner matrix; legal to request NDA for full SOC 2. We will follow up with a runbook and schedule the lab.
[42:20] Maya: Sounds good. One ask: can you include sample evidence file names and expected retention periods in the mapping doc?
[42:28] Jordan: Yes will include that.
[42:31] Olivia: From legal we'll want the chain of custody for evidence transfers.
[42:35] Luis: We'll include delivery notes and secure transfer methods (SFTP with MFA or signed link).
[42:42] Jordan: Any other blockers?
[42:44] Ethan: None from infra.
[42:46] Maya: No.
[42:47] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send notes and action items.
[42:52] [END]
